system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Penn National Gaming / Fontainebleau Las Vegas transaction, realized record (~2012-2014 window)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier contains no information about how
> the transaction was structured at closing. The outcome window was fixed at construction
> as the registrant's ~2012-2014 record (3-5 years after the ~2009 event).

## Consummation status governing the outcome
- No ownership boundary was crossed by the registrant: a competing bidder outbid the registrant's stalking-horse proposal and the registrant did not acquire the Fontainebleau Las Vegas asset. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-005666, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (press release dated February 4, 2010)]
- Because the proposed acquisition never closed, there is no acquired business to integrate and therefore no realized post-close integration trajectory to observe for this transaction. The outcome is accordingly coded UNCERTAIN / not-applicable (no realized integration record exists). [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-005666, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (press release dated February 4, 2010)]

## In-window primary record (confirming no integration outcome)
- The registrant's Form 10-K for fiscal 2013 (filed February 27, 2014), the annual report inside the fixed ~2012-2014 outcome window, contains no reference to "Fontainebleau" anywhere in the document, consistent with the registrant never having acquired or operated the asset. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-14-001467, Form 10-K (fiscal 2013)]
- Within that same annual report the registrant's Las Vegas-area property is identified as the M Resort in Henderson, Nevada (a separate property), further indicating that the unfinished Fontainebleau Project was not among the registrant's owned or operated assets during the outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-14-001467, Form 10-K (fiscal 2013)]

## Documented product/process/organization interface record
- Because no operating business, workforce, or process substrate was ever transferred to the registrant (the target was an unfinished, never-opened construction asset that was never acquired), there is no documented product/process interface record, process/organization interface record, or controlling-intent playout to report for this transaction. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-005666, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (press release dated February 4, 2010)]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The transaction produced no realized integration outcome for the registrant because it was never consummated: the registrant's stalking-horse bid was outbid at auction, no ownership boundary was crossed, and the registrant's own in-window fiscal-2013 annual report shows no Fontainebleau asset among its holdings. The outcome is coded UNCERTAIN / not-applicable (no public realized-integration record exists, because no acquisition occurred). [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-005666, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (press release dated February 4, 2010)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-14-001467, Form 10-K (fiscal 2013)]

[SLICE END]
